items.description: Those defending China and advancing Beijing’s false narratives for the sake of convenience will be made known to the Filipino people, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said yesterday.

items.title: Ex-BARMM lawmaker no-show at PDEA probe
items.description: Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang dodged a summons for him to appear on Thursday before the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), which sought to question him over a suspected half-ton shipment of shabu from Laos worth about P1.5 billion.

items.title: Nurse shortage could reach 250,000 by 2030 – CHED
items.description: The shortage of nurses could reach 250,000 by 2030 if current figures of 127,000 to 190,000 nurse deficit in 2025 continue, Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Chairperson Shirley Agrupis said yesterday.

items.title: VP’s SALN, AMLC records formally admitted into evidence
items.description: The Senate impeachment court has formally admitted into evidence the statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records of Vice President Sara Duterte, while denying the prosecution’s plea to include Commission on Audit (COA) reports regarding her controversial confidential funds.

items.title: Socmed affecting public perception of VP impeachment
items.description: Public opinion of the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte is largely affected by information being shared on social media, a political scientist said.

items.title: Make Christmas goods affordable, President Marcos tells execs
items.description: President Marcos has ordered government officials to make basic commodities affordable this Christmas season, while urging public institutions to keep holiday parties simple as the country prepares for the effects of a super El Niño.

items.title: Prosecution seeks protection for 55 witnesses in Duterte trial
items.description: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has formally requested judges to provide protective measures to 55 witnesses involved in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

items.title: NCRPO warns vs illegal water connections amid El Niño threat
items.description: The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) has ordered a crackdown on illegal water connections in Metro Manila, warning that unscrupulous groups are exploiting residents’ need for water amid concerns over supply shortages due to the El Niño phenomenon.

items.title: Palace wants deeper probe on Romualdez’s jail ‘assistant’
items.description: Malacañang wants a thorough investigation on alleged special treatment for President Marcos’ cousin and former speaker Martin Romualdez after a jail warden admitted that the lawmaker has a personal staff staying with him inside the New Quezon City Jail around the clock.

items.title: VP Sara leaves for Hong Kong
items.description: Vice President Sara Duterte left for Hong Kong yesterday where she is expected to stay until Nov. 8, a day before her defense team starts to present evidence in the ongoing impeachment trial against her.
